content.primary: あの ひと あの かた
content.secondary: That person, he, she (あの　かた　is the polite equivalent of あの　ひと）
content.reading: あの ひと あの かた

content.secondary: Mr., Ms. (suffix added to a name for expressing politeness)
(suffix often added to a child:s name instead of ~san)
teacher, instructor (not used when referring to one`s own job)
employee of ~ company (used with a company`s name)
who (どなた is the polite equivalent)
how old (おいくつ is the polite equivalent)
How do you do it? (lit. I am meeting you for the first time. Usually used as the first phrase when introducing oneself.)

content.primary: ［どうぞ］ よろしく ［お願いします］。
content.secondary: Pleased to meet you. (lit. Please be nice to me. Usually used at the end of a self-introduction.)
content.reading: ［どうぞ］ よろしく ［お願いします］。

content.secondary: Excuse me, but (used when asking someone for personal information such as their name or address)
Oh? What! (used when hearing something unexpected)
Here you are. (used when offering someone something)

content.primary: ［どうも］ ありがとう ［ございます］。
content.reading: ［どうも］ ありがとう ［ございます］。

content.secondary: Oh! (used when becoming aware of something)

content.primary: これから お世話に なります。
content.secondary: Thank you in advance for your kindness.
content.reading: これから お世話に なります。

content.primary: こちらこそ ［どうぞ］ よろしく ［お願いします］
content.secondary: Pleased to meet you, too. (response to ［どうぞ］　よろしく　［お願いします］）
content.reading: こちらこそ ［どうぞ］ よろしく ［お願いします］

content.secondary: there, that place near the listener
this way, this place (polite equivalent of ここ）
That way, that place near the listener (polite equivalent of そこ）
that way, that place over there (polite equivalent of あそこ）
which way, where (polite equivalent of どこ）
